chunks: Hariz narrated from Zurarah, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, concerning:

A man who recited aloud where it is not appropriate to recite aloud, or recited quietly where it is not appropriate to recite quietly — he said: whichever of the two he did deliberately, then he has invalidated his salat (prayer), and repetition is upon him. But if he did that forgetfully, absentmindedly, or without knowing, then there is nothing upon him, and his salat (prayer) is complete.

key_terms.الْإِجْهَارُ: audible recitation where the voice is raised

ai.seo_question: Does reciting aloud or quietly in the wrong part of salat invalidate the prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding jahr and ikhfa' in recitation during salat (prayer). Deliberately reciting aloud or quietly in the wrong place invalidates the prayer and requires repetition, while doing so out of forgetfulness, heedlessness, or ignorance does not incur liability and the prayer remains valid.
